node.label: Bruce G. Trigger
node.date_label: The Children of Aataentsic (1976) · Natives and Newcomers (1985) · A History of Archaeological Thought (1989)
node.description: A Canadian archaeologist and ethnohistorian of the Wendat (Huron) and of colonial encounters in northeastern North America. The Children of Aataentsic (1976) combines archaeology, history and ethnology to argue that Iroquoian societies had changed substantially in the centuries before European contact, so that the impact of contact cannot be assessed without understanding that earlier change. Natives and Newcomers (1985) reconsiders Canada’s ‘heroic age’ of exploration and colonization in the same way, and A History of Archaeological Thought (1989) is his history of his own discipline. He wrote the foreword to Georges E. Sioui’s For an Amerindian Autohistory (1992). Emma LaRocque criticizes that foreword as an example of containment, and argues that the cross-cultural approach to which Trigger belonged, though an improvement on earlier racist scholarship, could still distance and Other its subjects.
